title: Mixture of experts on four GPUs: tensor parallelism or expert parallelism
design_ref: Parallelism for MoE: expert parallelism, all-to-all and load balancing
purpose: Serve Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, 8 used per token) with TP4 and with four data-parallel engines sharing the experts (EP), read the engine's own account of the expert placement and the all-to-all, ask for expert load balancing, and compare goodput.

checks.description: under expert parallelism each of the four ranks holds a quarter of the 128 experts
checks.because: The engine prints its placement: 32 of 128 experts local to each rank. The attention layers are not sharded in this layout, so each GPU keeps its own copy of them and its own KV cache for its own requests.

checks.description: the all-to-all runs through all-gather and reduce-scatter (the PCIe-friendly path); the NVLink and InfiniBand kernels are not selected
checks.because: DeepEP's kernels need NVLink or RDMA hardware. The engine's default on this machine is the all-gather/reduce-scatter manager, so every token's activations visit every rank; the cost grows with batch, not with experts used.

checks.description: expert parallelism keeps more weights on each GPU than tensor parallelism does (attention is replicated)
checks.because: 5.15 GiB against 4.02 GiB per GPU: the experts are split four ways either way; only tensor parallelism also splits attention, embeddings and the shared layers.

checks.description: both sweeps ran: at the lightest level at least 90% of the offered requests completed on both layouts
checks.because: The lightest level is close to idle (0.02 requests per second per GPU), so it shows what one request costs on each layout; whether the targets are met at all is the finding, not a precondition.

checks.description: the two layouts compute the same model: at least 90% of their answers to 100 questions are identical
checks.because: Answers identical on 100% of questions. Different parallel layouts sum floating-point numbers in a different order, so a few answers can differ; a large disagreement would mean a wrong layout, not a different one.

checks.description: asking for expert load balancing on this checkpoint is refused by the engine with a clear message instead of being ignored
checks.because: Expert load balancing needs the model's expert layers to be replaceable at run time. The int4 (GPTQ) expert kernels this checkpoint uses are not, so the engine stops at start-up. The measurement of its effect needs a checkpoint in a format that supports it and more memory than a T4; it is therefore not made here.

notes: Near idle, chat ITL p95 is 23 ms with TP4 and 14 ms with four data-parallel engines and EP; the target is 150 ms. At least one layout meets the target near idle.

Not measured here: expert load balancing's effect (refused by the engine for this checkpoint, shown above); the DeepEP all-to-all kernels (need NVLink or RDMA); a multi-node wide expert-parallel layout (one GPU node).
